# plainkeep

> A personal operating system in a folder of plaintext. Markdown files in the user's own git repo hold knowledge (wiki), tasks, and a journal; one `plainkeep <verb>` command is the only writer. Two faces, one door: humans use `plainkeep ui` (a guided terminal UI generated from the machine contract), agents and scripts use `plainkeep <verb> --json` (a frozen envelope + exit-code protocol). A guardrail classifies every invocation (read / safe_write / draft_only / confirm / deny); nothing transmits without a human. No server, no daemon, no cloud. Python 3.10+ stdlib engine; optional layers (semantic search, local models, backups, scheduled jobs, the compiled terminal UI) are opt-in via a layered installer.

Key facts: the repo is a TEMPLATE — `script/get` clones a private copy (the vault, data-only) and installs the versioned, read-only ENGINE outside it (`~/.local/share/plainkeep/engine/<version>/`, ADR-017); `script/update` + `enginetree.py --update` stage, checksum, self-test, then switch one pointer, always retaining the previous pair for rollback (ADR-021), so user content is never touched. Automation is the DEFAULT offering (ADR-022): the setup wizard schedules the day's bookends (`start`, `close_nudge`) plus index/consolidate/organize_scan/backup_check; `plainkeep job set <name> --daily HH:MM` is a free vault write, `plainkeep job enable/disable --yes` is the confirm-class activation into launchd, and `plainkeep job status` reports rendered/installed/loaded + drift separately. The generated `plainkeep.json` (schema `plainkeep.json/3`) describes the entire verb surface: args, output schemas, risk classes, per-action grammar (`actions[]` with typed args + completion providers), and capabilities. Exit codes are a protocol: 0 ok · 2 usage · 3 needs --yes · 4 not found · 5 denied — refusal messages carry the exact corrected command ("refusals teach"). `plainkeep mcp` is a stateless MCP stdio server whose tool list is generated from plainkeep.json; every tool call shells back through `plainkeep <verb> --json`, so the guardrail and logs remain the single enforcement path. Four roots: the vault, `~/work` (code, separate repos), `~/files` (binary assets, restic-backed), `~/dotfiles`.

This site has four pages: [/](https://plainkeep.vercel.app/) (overview + install), [/how-it-works](https://plainkeep.vercel.app/how-it-works) (command anatomy, the enforcement path, safety classes), [/features](https://plainkeep.vercel.app/features) (every capability incl. the schedule), [/agents](https://plainkeep.vercel.app/agents) (the agent contract, MCP, the rules agents follow).

All links below are raw markdown — fetch them directly.

## Start here

- [README](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gabros20/plainkeep/main/README.md): what plainkeep is, quick start, the verb surface, guardrail classes, agent wiring, project layout
- [Layered setup](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gabros20/plainkeep/main/docs/setup.md): the `plainkeep setup` installer — wizard, dashboard, all six layers (skeleton, search, backups, models, automation, ui), status enum, agent rules
- [Docs map](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gabros20/plainkeep/main/docs/README.md): every doc, organized by reader intent

## The contracts (for agents)

- [Machine contract](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gabros20/plainkeep/main/docs/machine-contract.md): the normative reference — `--json` envelope, exit-code protocol, `--dry-run` semantics, `plainkeep.json/3` schema, `cmd.json` sidecar, `actions[]` grammar, completion contract
- [Agent contract](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gabros20/plainkeep/main/AGENTS.md): the operating contract any agent reads before driving the vault
- [Operating manual](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gabros20/plainkeep/main/skills/operate-plainkeep/SKILL.md): the detailed skill — orientation ritual, verb reference, provenance rules, what agents must never do

## Understanding the system

- [Architecture](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gabros20/plainkeep/main/docs/architecture.md): why the system is shaped this way — principles, the one-door enforcement path, trade-offs, frontends
- [Decision log](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gabros20/plainkeep/main/docs/DECISIONS.md): the ADR record of every load-bearing decision, including rejected alternatives
- [Changelog](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gabros20/plainkeep/main/CHANGELOG.md): what changed and when

## Capabilities

- [The terminal UI](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gabros20/plainkeep/main/docs/terminal-ui.md): install, use, and update `plainkeep ui` — the contract-generated human face, shipped as a compiled binary
- [Plugins](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gabros20/plainkeep/main/docs/plugins.md): write your own verbs against the frozen SDK; the install + trust model for packs
- [Backup & share](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gabros20/plainkeep/main/docs/backup-and-share.md): the restic backup family (append-only cloud key) and capability-URL sharing
- [Agent-readable shares](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gabros20/plainkeep/main/docs/share-agent-markdown.md): how a shared link serves raw markdown to any agent's fetch tool
- [Obsidian compatibility](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gabros20/plainkeep/main/docs/obsidian-compat.md): the normative emit/tolerate definition for the zero-cost frontend
